title: End-to-end latency profiling traces: March 2026 run
content:
Purpose:
This doc contains the raw traces and a short analysis from the end-to-end latency profiling run on 2026-03-25 -> 2026-03-26. Goal was to measure tail latency (p50/p95/p99) and per-stage breakdowns for our standard inference path (hosted API -> routing -> runtime -> model inference -> post-processing). Test harness and config are listed, followed by aggregated latency percentiles and representative per-request stage traces.

Test environment:
- Model: llama2-13b-ctx512 (q4_0 quantized variant used in Dedicated perf profile)
- Hardware: 2x A100-80GB per shard, inference runtime pinned to GPU-local placement
- Workload: seq_len=512 tokens, generate up to 128 tokens, temperature=0.0, batch_size=1, concurrency sweep [1, 4, 8, 16] (we include the 1 and 8 runs here)
- Network: intra-region (us-west-2) with average RTT ~3.5ms; client simulated from same VPC to minimize network jitter
- Warmup: 600 warmup requests, measurement window 10k requests per configuration

High-level aggregated numbers (single-shard, batch=1, concurrency=8 run):
- end-to-end latency (incl. client->edge routing->runtime->post):
  - p50: 112 ms
  - p95: 238 ms
  - p99: 412 ms
- runtime-only (time spent inside serving runtime process, excludes network and API gateway):
  - p50: 78 ms
  - p95: 180 ms
  - p99: 345 ms

Per-stage median breakdown (p50) - typical request (all numbers in ms):
- client->edge (network + gateway): 8
- request-routing + auth checks: 6
- request-deserialization + tokenization: 12
- kv-cache lookup (prefix cache hit): 4
- model-inference (forward + kv updates): 42
- post-processing (detokenize + safety filter + response serialization): 8
- edge egress: 2
- total (p50): 82 ms runtime portion + 30 ms external = ~112 ms total

Per-stage tail behaviors (p95 / p99):
- request-routing spikes (p99 routing stage): up to 95 ms observed for ~0.6% of requests — correlated with brief under-provisioning of route-controller pod during rollout (see linked ENG-2476).
- tokenization: p99 occasionally shows +45ms overhead for very long inputs (>480 tokens) due to fallback to slower tokenization path in the tokenizer library.
- model-inference: dominates tail — p95 166 ms, p99 320 ms. Two sub-causes identified:
  1) kernel warm-up / context switch when GPU is handling a different sequence length on previous request (observed in traces where preceding request had seq_len=1024 on a different job).
  2) periodic GC on CPU-side pre/post-processing thread pool, causing delays of 30–80ms that propagate into inference scheduling.
- KV-cache miss penalty: when cache miss falls back to full KV reconstruction we see +60–120ms on p99 for those requests. Cache miss rate in this run ~1.8% (higher than usual because we cleared cache between shard restarts).

Representative trace samples (timestamps are relative to request arrival; times in ms):
- Example (p50 request):
  0.0 request-received
  6.2 routing/auth
  18.5 tokenization
  22.9 kv-cache-lookup (hit)
  65.1 model-inference (start)
  107.3 model-inference (end)
  115.0 post-processing
  117.2 response-sent
  total: 117.2 ms

- Example (p99 request - cache miss + routing spike):
  0.0 request-received
  42.0 routing/auth (spike)
  54.4 tokenization (long input fallback)
  56.1 kv-cache-lookup (miss) -> full KV reconstruction + 82.6 ms
  245.8 model-inference (start)
  566.3 model-inference (end)
  601.0 post-processing (GC pause observed before serialization)
  total: 610.2 ms

Trace-level notes and observations:
- The dominant contributor to p99 is model-inference and cache-miss reconstruction. When cache is warm and hits are high, p99 drops ~120ms on average.
- Short-lived routing-controller rollout coincided with routing stage spike; that improved after locking a stable replica set (see ENG-2476).
- The tokenizer fallback path appears on long inputs; we should quantify how often production inputs >480 tokens occur and whether we can eliminate fallback by pre-compiling a fast path.
- There is measurable correlation between GC activity on CPU worker threads and jitter in inference scheduling; GC windows correspond to 20–90ms extra latency in several traces.

Quick experiments run during the session:
1) Disabled CPU-side safety filter on a subset of requests -> median runtime reduced by ~6ms, p95 reduced by ~12ms. Safety filter is cheap but runs on main thread; moving to off-thread execution or a faster implementation would reduce tail.
2) Kept KV-cache pinned across restarts -> cache miss rate dropped from 1.8% -> 0.2% and p99 reduced by ~85ms. This confirms cache miss penalty cost.
3) Added a tiny pre-warm micro-batch for GPU kernels (send 4 synthetic requests every 10s) -> slight reduction in p99 (about 20–30ms) but increased noise; needs more controlled validation.

Action items / next steps:
- (Avery) Create follow-up PR to move safety filter to off-thread execution (PR#582).
- (Miguel) Investigate tokenizer fallback and prepare perf micro-benchmark for long inputs; log stats on prod for 2 weeks to estimate frequency.
- (Priya) Add metrics to trace kv-cache lifecycle so we can detect cache cold starts and attribute tail spikes automatically.
- (Eng-SRE) Stabilize route-controller rollout strategy; add gradual-bounce policy to avoid 1–2 minute spikes during deploys.

Appendix: raw trace dump (trimmed) - sample request IDs and per-stage durations:
- req: ab12f4 | routing: 5.9 | tokenization: 11.8 | kv: 3.9 | inference: 41.2 | post: 7.4 | total: 70.2
- req: ab12f5 | routing: 43.1 | tokenization: 12.3 | kv: miss(82.6) | inference: 320.5 | post: 8.1 | total: 466.6
- req: ab12f6 | routing: 6.0 | tokenization: 12.6 | kv: 4.1 | inference: 39.8 | post: 6.9 | total: 68.0

If you want the full raw CSV of traces (10k rows) I can attach it or push to the shared profiling bucket.

Notes on provenance: trace runner: tools/perf/e2e-tracer v0.9.2; runtime build: serving-runtime@release-2026-03-15; kernels: cudnn/8.6 tuned.

-- end of run report --
